- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical lows after initial spikes.
- Forecast accuracy degrades as horizon extends beyond 10–15 days, with later days showing larger errors.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting lag in capturing downward trends.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust downward — possibly due to delayed reaction to market signals.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections in the last 5–10 days, especially after a spike.
- Forecasts should be capped at historical 30-day moving average to prevent over-optimism.
- Adjust for recent downward momentum — if last 5 days show decline, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- Avoid extrapolating from recent spikes — if price spiked >10% from 10-day average, reduce forecast by 15–20%.
